tools.name: blender_execute_python
tools.title: Run Python (bpy) inside the user's Blender
tools.description: Executes Python code in the user's running Blender with the bpy API available and returns what it printed plus the value of a variable named `result` if you set one. This is how you build or edit the scene: add primitives, set transforms, materials, lights, cameras, keyframes, modifiers, import files. Runs on the user's machine with their permissions — keep it to scene work, never touch files outside Blender's own data. Prefer several small calls over one huge script; each call has 3 minutes. Undo is available to the user (Ctrl+Z) for what you change. A video model later copies what the playblast shows - shapes, silhouettes and surface patterns - so build volume, not texture: smooth-shaded primitives, no Displace or noise surfaces, thickness for fins, wings and leaves (never one flat polygon); materials and fine detail belong in the video prompt. Large flat walls come back as giant blank windows: break facades into rough floors, windows and doors, or describe the facade in the prompt. Keep the blockout primitive and in clay: build only what sets the camera, the composition, the scale and the motion - heroes as stand_in() figures (one smooth body with a nose for facing, no costume, hair or props), vehicles as vehicle() (real size, one object), the route as volumes, the road or track as a raised ribbon; leave out extras and crowds, plants, rocks, small props, anything handled (a ball, a bottle, a phone), any keyed prop and any textured model, and write them in the prompt with their physics - approach, contact, force, recovery (mira-blender-scene skill, references/blockout.md) - whatever you build comes back looking the way it was built. An animated creature must bend, not glide: after keying its path run bpy.ops.mira.flex_creature(target=name) (spine arch along the path, tail strokes, a squash where it lands), and let a leaping or falling body roll around its long axis rather than bank like an aircraft. A person lifted, carried or thrown is stand_in(pose="limp") held by its middle with limbs and head hanging, never a straight figure spinning (it comes back as a diver); runners react before they run and build speed over 1-1.5 s (run_path(), built into agent scripts with stand_in(), vehicle() and creature()), never full speed on the first frame. Everything is recorded in clay, vehicles too - the prompt names their colour - and vehicles roll on their wheels: hops, bounces and rocking go in the prompt. A few lane marks or posts show scale and speed. The camera move is camera_move(name, target=..., size=...) (add-on 0.13.0+, built into agent scripts): the moves of Mira's camera bank built on a rig the way their guards say - push_in, dolly_in/out, truck_left/right, pedestal_up/down, crane_up/down, slider_short, pan_left/right, tilt_up/down, whip_pan, arc_left/right, orbit_360, zoom_in/out, fast_zoom, crash_zoom(_out), dolly_zoom, rack_focus, tracking_side, tracking_reverse, follow_ots, handheld_raw, handheld_follow, locked_off, lazy_susan; size is metres, degrees or (from, to) field of view, and at=frame puts a quick beat (a crash zoom's snap, a whip pan) on its action (0.14.0+). The playblast facts then name the move, and the prompt carries the bank's description of it; they also measure every shot's camera whatever keyed it - drift under 0.3 m reads as locked off, so key a real move or none - its zooms, the shot size, who enters the frame and where each stand-in faces. Lock the camera before lighting: key (named LGT_key), fill, rim, each for a reason - the clip records clay under studio light, so the facts describe the scene's light to the prompt in words.

code.description: Python source. `bpy`, `bmesh`, `mathutils` and `math` are already imported.

label.description: Short label shown to the user in the add-on's activity log, e.g. 'add subway car blockout'.

annotations.title: Run Python (bpy) inside the user's Blender

tools.name: save_blogger
tools.title: Save a draft as an AI Blogger
tools.description:
Turns a finished draft into a saved AI BLOGGER: renders its full canon - the reference views the platform uses to keep the face and body identical everywhere, about 7-8 minutes - and auto-designs a first voice from its traits. SPENDS 45 CREDITS (the first voice is included). BEFORE calling, tell the user it costs 45 credits and get an explicit yes in this conversation; never save on your own initiative. Saving the same draft again returns the same blogger without a second charge.
Returns the blogger - status 'generating' until the canon is done; list_brand_assets kind 'avatar' shows 'ready' - and up to three voice previews: let the user listen and pin one with set_blogger_voice generatedVoiceId. Once ready, its blogger_id goes as bloggerId into generate_image, generate_video, extend_video, generate_3d, direct_video, blogger_motion, blogger_speak, motion_control, recast_video, avatar_video, generate_audio and voiceover_video.

tools.name: adobe_beat_markers
tools.title: Find the beat of a music layer and mark it
tools.description: Analyses the music layer of an After Effects composition on the user's machine (tempo, a steady beat grid, 4/4 downbeats, drops where the bar gets louder or the kick doubles, low/mid/high sections) and writes composition markers 'mira:bar 5', 'mira:beat 12', 'mira:drop' (Mira's own markers are replaced, the user's stay). Returns bpm, grid_offset and beat_seconds (beat k is at grid_offset + k * beat_seconds in composition time), downbeats, drops and sections: cut, place transitions (whoosh 0.3-0.5 s before a cut, riser 1-2 s before a drop) and time animation to them. When the tempo is a half, double or triplet feel of what you expect, pass bpmHint (e.g. the BPM you asked generate_audio for) or one of `alternatives`. downbeats are a best guess; the grid is the reliable part. In Premiere Pro (panel 0.9.5+) it reads the music clip on an audio track (`track`, default 1 = A2; `clip`, default the longest) and writes sequence markers with the same names, times in sequence seconds. Spends no credits.

layer.description: Layer name or 1-based index of the music; omit for the first layer with audio.

comp.description: Composition name; omit for the active one.

mode.description: downbeats (default) | beats | every (every N beats) | drops | none (analysis only).

every.description: For mode 'every': a marker every N beats (default 2).

bpmHint.description: Expected tempo; the search stays within 8 % of it.

track.description: Premiere: 0-based audio track of the music (default 1 = A2).

clip.description: Premiere: the music clip on that track, 0-based index or exact name (default the longest).

annotations.title: Find the beat of a music layer and mark it

tools.name: create_blogger_draft
tools.title: Draft a new AI Blogger
tools.description:
Renders a DRAFT of a new AI BLOGGER - ONE 3:2 image: a portrait on the left and the full body on the right, on white - from traits (ids from list_blogger_traits), an optional description, optional real face photos (1-4 of one person) and an optional style reference. SPENDS 8 CREDITS per draft - say so before the first one. Takes about 60-110 s; at most 2 drafts render at once per account.
Flow: list_blogger_traits -> agree the look with the user -> this -> wait_for_generation -> show the image -> refine with another call (previousDraftId = this draft's generation_id plus editText, e.g. 'shorter hair, a warmer smile': the rest and the face are kept) or roll new traits with randomize -> when the user is happy, save_blogger (45 credits, ask first). A draft is not a saved blogger: only blogger_motion and blogger_speak take it (draftId) as a test drive.
With photoUrls the face comes from the photos, and gender, age and hair too unless traits name them; still pass gender as seen in the photos - save_blogger matches the blogger's voice to it.
photoUrls and styleReferenceUrl must be the user's own files - upload_reference_image / create_upload URLs or their Mira images; any other link is refused before a credit is spent. Base a blogger on a real face only when it is the user's own face or the person agreed.

traits.description: Chosen traits as {sectionId: [optionId, ...]} with ids from list_blogger_traits, e.g. {"character_type":["average"],"gender":["female"],"render":["photoreal"]}. One id per section unless the section is multi (features up to 3, distinctive up to 2, accessories up to 3). Sections left out take their defaults. With randomize=true the sections passed here are kept and the rest is rolled. With previousDraftId and no traits the previous draft's traits are kept.

description.description: What traits cannot say, in English, up to 400 characters: 'a thin scar over the left brow, always in a yellow raincoat'.

editText.description: Only with previousDraftId: what to change in that draft, up to 200 characters, e.g. 'make the hair shorter and the jacket red'. Everything else is kept.

photoUrls.description: 1-4 URLs of photos of ONE person to base the blogger on - the user's uploads (upload_reference_image) or Mira images; more angles keep the face closer. Only with character_type 'average'; never with creatures.

photoUrl.description: One face photo URL - the same as a single item of photoUrls (kept for older clients).

styleReferenceUrl.description: URL of an image whose look and drawing style to follow - the user's upload or Mira image.

previousDraftId.description: generation_id of an earlier SUCCEEDED draft to refine (with editText). Its traits and face photos carry over unless you pass new ones.

randomize.description: true to roll random traits (Shuffle); the sections passed in traits stay as they are.

tools.name: generate_3d
tools.title: Generate a 3D model
tools.description:
Creates a textured 3D mesh (GLB, plus FBX/OBJ/USDZ where the model offers them) from a text prompt, from ONE photo, or from up to four photos of the same object (multi-view). SPENDS THE USER'S CREDITS: 4 to 50 per model and quality tier, plus add-ons for PBR maps, rigging and animation clips - call list_models for the exact table and say the price before running.
Describe ONE physical object in English: category first (a humanoid character, a creature, a vehicle, a prop, a piece of furniture), then silhouette, parts and their proportions, the material and colour of each part. No scene, camera, lighting or mood - none of it exists in a mesh. Characters that will be rigged: ask for a symmetrical A-pose, arms away from the body, legs apart, nothing overlapping the body. Pass skill='3d' to get the playbook's doctrine.
Photos: one clean shot of a single object on a plain background works best; the platform removes busy backgrounds for the photo-only models. For multi-view send the views in the order front, back, left, right.
Generation is asynchronous: this returns a generation_id immediately. Poll get_generation or call wait_for_generation; the result carries the GLB url first and every extra file (FBX, OBJ, USDZ, rigged model, animation clips, textures) in files[].

prompt.description: Object description in English (see the tool description). Optional when photos are given - then it only guides the texture on models that read it.

model.description:
3D model to use. Pick by what the asset is FOR; leave empty for 'hunyuan-3.1'.
'hunyuan-3.1' (Hunyuan3D 3.1 Pro; in: text+photo(4); out: glb/fbx/obj/usdz; credits: draft 8, standard 14, high 19; PBR +6) - the default: the best geometry-per-credit for both text and photo (~13 credits), FBX/OBJ/USDZ next to the GLB, PBR maps on request (+5), multi-view reconstruction from up to four photos (+5). Pick it for any prop, product, vehicle, creature or environment piece and for characters that will be rigged afterwards with rig_3d. A geometry-only draft tier exists (~8).
'meshy-7' (Meshy 7; in: text+photo(4); out: glb/fbx/obj/usdz; credits: draft 29, standard 43, high 50; inline rig +8) - the character model: humanoid rig plus walking/running clips inline (~42 + 7 credits) and up to ten extra animation presets, quad or low-poly game topology, A/T-pose control, the richest textures; the most expensive of the four. Pick it when the asset must be rigged, animated or game-ready; for a plain prop hunyuan-3.1 does the same for a third of the price.
'trellis-2' (Trellis 2; in: photo(4); out: glb; credits: draft 9, standard 11, high 13) - photo-to-3D for props and products: the cleanest geometry and UV layout in its price band (~11 credits), best when the user has a good photo of a single object; no text input, no FBX/USDZ (GLB only), no rigging. Needs a clean subject - the platform removes the background first. Not for characters that must be rigged.
'rodin-fast' (Rodin Gen-2.5 Fast; in: text+photo(5); out: glb/fbx/obj/usdz/stl; credits: draft 4, standard 4, high 4) - the cheapest and fastest model (~4 credits), any output format including STL for printing and FBX/USDZ for engines; geometry is coarse, textures are simple - use it for a quick draft of the shape, a first look at a concept, a print-only piece, or when the user explicitly wants a specific format cheaply. Not for hero assets.
Rigging any finished GLB afterwards (rig_3d): 8 credits + 5 per animation clip.

referenceImageUrls.description: Public HTTPS URLs of reference photos of the object, at most 4. One photo = image-to-3D; several = multi-view (order: front, back, left, right).

quality.description: Quality tier: 'draft' (quick, cheap, checks the shape), 'standard' (default), 'high' (the model's top geometry/texture setting).

topology.description: Mesh topology: 'triangle' (detailed, default), 'quad' (smooth, animation-friendly) or 'lowpoly' (game asset; meshy-7 only). Leave empty for the model's default.

format.description: Primary output format: 'glb' (default, always produced), 'fbx', 'obj', 'usdz' or 'stl' - only where the model lists it (see list_models formats).

pbr.description: true to add PBR maps (metallic, roughness, normal) on models that support it. Costs extra on hunyuan-3.1.

rig.description: true to auto-rig a HUMANOID character (Meshy rigging): returns a rigged GLB and FBX with free walking and running clips. Costs extra. Only for characters with clearly defined limbs - never for props.

animationIds.description: Meshy animation preset ids to bake as clips against the rig (at most 10). Presets: 0=Idle, 30=Walk, 106=Confident walk, 14=Run, 16=Sprint, 466=Jump, 13=Running jump, 28=Wave hello, 25=Nod yes, 298=Cheer, 4=Attack, 96=Punch, 103=Kick, 87=Boxing, 8=Death, 33=Sit (chair), 22=Funny dance, 64=Dance. Leave empty for the rig alone (walking and running clips come free with every rig).

heightMeters.description: Character height in meters for rigging (default 1.7).

pose.description: Pose for characters: 'a-pose' or 't-pose'. Leave empty for props.

tools.name: blender_playblast
tools.title: Record the user's viewport animation as a reference clip
tools.description: Renders the viewport (or scene camera) animation to a clean 1280x720 clip on the user's machine, uploads it to their Mira library and returns its URL, ready for referenceVideoUrls in generate_video (seedance-2-5, minimax, wan3, wan3-prime, kling, kling-motion, omni) - pass ratio '16:9' with it, the clip is landscape and the models default to 9:16. Keep the range short: models take 3-30 s of reference; the tool refuses more than 30 s. By default figures keep travelling and turning but their gestures hold still (Seedance repeats moving limbs beat for beat) and the clip is painted in neutral clay, so colours, materials and outfits come from your prompt: bind the clip to the camera path, the framing and roughly where the characters stand and move, say the figures in the clip (mannequins, capsules or 3D models, whatever they look like) are only stand-ins whose poses and gestures are not copied, and describe what the characters do and how they look in the style you want (live action, anime, cartoon, 3D animation). Never ask for 'the framing at each moment' or 'the position of every character' and do not time the actions to the clip. freezeFigures=false keeps the keyed motion, which the model copies closely - only for exact choreography or kling-motion. Capsule and mannequin figures are fine for Seedance (only a photoreal person who is not one of the account's AI Bloggers is refused). The result lists warnings about blockout surfaces and parts the model would copy literally (noisy faceted surfaces, flat single-polygon parts of moving figures): fix them and record again before generate_video. Camera markers bound to cameras (scene.timeline_markers, marker.camera) cut between cameras inside one clip; the result's facts list the shots with timecodes and each figure's place per shot - write one SHOT line per shot with those timecodes. People in a collection named Crowd (or marked mira_crowd) close to a shot's camera are left out of the clip and far ones stay as a density cue: facts.crowd counts them and names where they stand - write the crowd into the prompt. facts.movers lists the vehicles and creatures that travel with their class, top speed, braking and tilt; figures carry top speed and time in the air - write the mechanism or the gait from those numbers. A rigid creature needs bpy.ops.mira.flex_creature before you record. The result's `clause` is the sentence block to carry in the prompt with the clip. When the scene still has extras, a crowd, plants, rocks, a handled prop (a ball, a bottle, a phone), a keyed prop, a textured model, a field of look-alike blocks away from the cameras (build the route, write the district), a bouncing vehicle or the scene's own colours, the tool does not record: it returns blocked=true and `stops` - fix each one and record again; pass force=true only when the user explicitly insists.

throughCamera.description: true = render through the scene camera; false (default) = the user's viewport.

freezeFigures.description: true (default) = figures keep travelling and turning as a whole but their limbs, heads and bones hold still, so the model plays the gestures from your prompt. false = every keyed motion stays and the model copies it closely.

look.description: How the clip is painted: clay (default) = every object one neutral clay colour, so the model takes shapes, placement and camera and gets colours, materials and outfits from your prompt; ids = each figure its own flat label colour, the rest clay; scene = the scene's own colours - not for video: flat viewport colours come back as game-like surfaces and plastic parts.

tools.description:
MIRACLE (the Miracle tab of AI Bloggers): in a 3-30 s clip, replaces the PEOPLE (with the user's AI Blogger or a photo), an OUTFIT, a PRODUCT, the PLACE or a SIGN while the motion, camera, timing and the clip's own SOUND stay; on Seedance it can also REDRAW the whole clip in a STYLE, ADD up to 2 people and end with a LINE the AI Blogger says. Call miracle_analyze first and pass its analysisId: it gives the people (personId p1...), the objects (objectId o1...), the styles and the engines this clip can run on with their price and photo limit.
ENGINES: 'seedance' (Seedance 2.5, the DEFAULT, 10 credits per second, 720p) - the whole clip (4-30 s) in ONE pass, a photo limit for the WHOLE clip; offered when miracle_analyze lists it. 'kling' (Kling 3.0 Omni, 6 credits per second, 1080p) - the clip goes in parts of up to 10 s stitched back into one, a photo limit PER PART, photos of real people allowed. A real person's photo goes in the one pass when miracle_analyze shows real_person_photos: true for seedance; otherwise the run goes in parts on kling. engine 'auto' (default) takes seedance when the clip has it and it takes this cast, otherwise kling - quote the price of the engine the run will take. style and addPeople work ONLY on seedance: with them a clip seedance cannot take is refused (miracle_seedance_required) and engine 'kling' is not allowed.
mode 'transfer' (default, motion transfer): the cast, the place and the look are rebuilt from the references - the new people perform the clip's motion, optionally in a new place (locationUrl). mode 'swap': only what you name changes, everything else in frame stays as it was.
cast: [{personId, bloggerId | photoUrl}] - people left out stay as they are. swaps: [{target 'outfit' | 'product' | 'location' | 'text', objectId?, what?, text? (target 'text': the new lettering), imageUrls? (1-4 photos, required for every target but 'text')}].
Photos count towards the engine's limit from miracle_analyze - on kling per part: the people visible in that part (an AI Blogger counts as one) + the place + the swap photos; on seedance for the whole clip. Photos must be the user's own files - upload_reference_image / create_upload URLs or Mira images; any other link is refused before a credit is spent. A REAL person's photo needs consent=true: ask the user to confirm the people in the photos are them or agreed - never assume it.
style: one of the ids from miracle_analyze (anime, cartoon_3d, clay, comic, watercolor, oil_painting, sketch, pixel_art, noir, retro_film) and/or styleImageUrl - redraws the whole clip, every move and cut kept; it can go with cast and addPeople in the same pass. addPeople: [{bloggerId | photoUrl, position?, action?}], up to 2 - people who were not in the clip, placed and acting as told.

It adds speech and lipsync to the price (estimate_cost kind 'miracle' with chars). If the lipsync fails the video comes without the line and its part of the price is refunded.

SPENDS CREDITS PER SECOND of the clip at the chosen engine's rate - quote the exact price miracle_analyze gives for that engine (or estimate_cost kind 'miracle', model = the engine, sourceSeconds, chars = the line) and get a yes. Renders in about 5-8 minutes into one video with the clip's sound (keepSound=false drops it). Returns a generation_id; call wait_for_generation.

tools.name: generate_video
tools.title: Generate a video clip
tools.description:
Renders a short video clip from a text prompt, or animates a reference image. SPENDS THE USER'S CREDITS, and video is far more expensive than an image - the price depends on model, duration and resolution. Always tell the user which model you picked and that it will spend credits BEFORE calling this.
Write the whole clip prompt in English as plain cinematic prose, not hand-assembled model syntax: a pipeline of specialists (cast and blocking, scene and props, camera, light, look and sound) emits the model's native format itself. YOUR DECISIONS ARE LAW - whatever you state explicitly, a camera move, a lighting scheme, an action, a spoken line, is kept word for word, and the pipeline only fills the slots you left empty. Carry the hard facts INTO the prose: spoken lines word for word, on-screen text exactly, the product named as a thing visible in shot.
Video takes several minutes. This returns a generation_id immediately; poll get_generation or call wait_for_generation, which may need several calls before the clip is ready.

prompt.description: The complete clip prompt in English - cinematic prose, not model syntax.

model.description:
Model to render the clip. CHOOSE ONE DELIBERATELY, BY WHAT THE CLIP NEEDS.
SELECTION RULE - apply it every single call:
1. Name the ONE thing that decides this clip: speech on camera? a person handling the product? readable text or Cyrillic in frame? several people at once? an edit of a clip that already exists? forceful camera work or a tightly sequenced set of moves and beats? If one of these is true, take the model listed for it below.
2. If NONE of them is true - a SIMPLE SHORT clip, b-roll, a variant, a draft - the choice is between two, by what the clip is FOR:
   'omni' is the working answer. Cheapest of the lineup, and it directs its own MULTI-SHOT - which is most of why it is the default, because a clip that cuts beats a clip that holds one slow frame. It also renders on-frame text well and is the only model that can edit a clip that already exists. The price of that: you cannot pin its duration - it picks its own 3-10s - and it does not take 1:1.
   'veo-quality' when this clip is the HERO - the launch film, the one visual the campaign rests on - and cinematic realism is the point. Fixed 8s, roughly four times the price. Finals only, never drafts, never volume runs. It shoots ONE UNBROKEN TAKE: it cannot cut. If the hero brief has cuts, a chase or a launch stride, rule 1 already sent it to 'runway' or 'seedance-2-5' - being the hero does not override that.
3. 'seedance-2-5' is the answer when LENGTH or REFERENCING decides the clip: 10, 15 or 30 seconds, heavy reference volume, or an attached avatar that has to reach the model as an identity - it is the only family with that transport, and on every other key an attached avatar is rebuilt into a synthetic start frame instead.
4. 'minimax' is a PURPOSE model for speech, Cyrillic and legible in-frame text - the only one that holds all three. It is NOT a general default. If you cannot say in one clause why this specific clip needs it, you do not need it.
5. Never repeat the same key call after call out of habit - re-read the brief each time.
'seedance-2-5' - the long-form specialist: up to 30s, heavy referencing (storyboards, keyframe chains, video edit/extend); pricier than any Veo tier - reach for it only when length or reference volume decides the clip. ALSO the camera-trick model WITH audio: in live runs (2026-09-06) it executed every phased single-take trick as written - a top-down crash dive, a full 360 orbit returning to the start, a whip pan fusing two locations, a dolly zoom, a camera struck and falling while it records, a locked day-night cycle, a pass through a mirror into a new place - where Runway smeared or split half of them and Kling stopped short of the move; when the MOVE is the concept and the clip needs sound, this is the key | video refs: up to 10 clips, 30 s each (motion/camera/pacing, never identity); a clip with a photoreal person who is not one of the account's avatars is REFUSED by the provider - blockout figures, stylised characters, products, places and objects go through
'runway' - Gen-4.5, text-to-video AND image-to-video: the sequencing specialist - executes several ordered camera moves and timed beats inside ONE prompt, and takes forceful camera work (sweeping arcs, crash zooms, whip pans) the others smear; weak on fine motor detail; NO audio; 720p; 5/10s
'kling' - best human anatomy and physics (sport, cloth, water), legible in-frame text, native audio with multi-speaker dialogue and accents; 3-15s; 1080p output | video refs: up to 1 clips, 10 s each (motion/camera/pacing, never identity)
'kling-turbo' - the faster, cheaper Kling 3.0: ONE continuous take from text or a single start frame, native audio always on; 3-15s; 1080p; no reference photos, clips, end frames or multi-shot - for those use kling
'kling-motion' - motion transfer: ONE photo of a character + ONE driving video (3-30 s, one person, single take) - the character in the photo performs the motion of the video; output length = video length; 1080p; keeps the clip's original sound. The only model that copies choreography exactly. Needs both inputs - refuse without a video | REQUIRES exactly 1 reference clip (3-30 s) + 1 photo; output length = clip length
'veo' - premium cinematography with native synchronized audio at a fair price; fixed 8s; keep to 1-2 subjects; attaching references locks the clip to 8s
'veo-lite' - the cheap Veo: same 8s audio clips at a fraction of the price, but NO reference images - drafts, b-roll, volume runs
'veo-quality' - the flagship Veo for hero clips: top cinematic realism at ~3x the Fast price - finals only, never drafts. ONE UNBROKEN TAKE: it cannot cut, so a brief with cuts, a chase or a launch stride is not its brief even when it is the hero
'omni' - self-directing storyteller and the only model that can EDIT an existing clip: multi-shots by default, renders on-frame text well, chooses its own 3-10s length (you cannot pin the duration); up to 6 photo refs and first/last frame anchors, but NO clip input at all - its video port is closed on our key
'minimax' - the purpose model for SPEECH plus legible/Cyrillic in-frame text - the only one holding both; millisecond-precise shot timing; 4-15s; NOT a general default | video refs: up to 3 clips, 15 s each (motion/camera/pacing, never identity)
'happyhorse' - dialogue-first with 7-language lip-sync; single-beat clips and exotic vertical ratios; briefs must stay tiny; ONE photo only - the nine-reference route exists but is not paid on our key
'wan3' - the long-take model: 30 seconds in ONE continuous generation, so a whole story keeps one look and one cast - no stitching; shot-numbered storyboard with timecodes, native audio, 10 photo refs; 2-30s; 1080p | video refs: up to 5 clips, 15 s each (motion/camera/pacing, never identity)
'wan3-prime' - the accelerated Wan 3.0: the same long take (30 seconds in ONE generation, one look and one cast), the same shot-numbered storyboard, native audio and 10 photo refs, rendered several times faster; ~1.4x the price of wan3; 2-30s; 1080p | video refs: up to 5 clips, 15 s each (motion/camera/pacing, never identity)
Leave empty only if nothing above fits - it then falls back to 'seedance-2-5'.

style.description: Optional render style, same meaning as for images: 'anime', 'render3d', 'pixel'. Leave EMPTY for a photographic clip.

skill.description:
Optional SKILL - a playbook for the genre and structure of the piece (not its medium; medium is `style`). The platform injects the playbook's doctrine into its prompt pipeline itself, so never restate or paraphrase it: pass the id and write the piece as the user described it. Pick by what the piece is FOR:
'ugc' (both) - UGC: A real person shows or talks about a product the way a customer would: a review, an unboxing, a short how-to, a testimonial, a "day with it" clip. Vertical, social, meant to sit between other people's phone videos and not stand out as paid.
'product' (both) - Product: A packshot, a product video, a marketplace card, a lifestyle scene where the product is in use but still the hero. Anything where a buyer needs to see exactly what they get.
'ads' (both) - Ads: Paid social creative, a launch teaser, a sale announcement, a static banner with a headline. The piece exists to make someone act, not to be admired.
'cinematic' (both) - Cinematic: A brand film, a teaser, a hero shot, a key visual, an atmospheric moment with a person, a place or a product. The piece is meant to be felt before it is understood.
'explainer' (video) - Explainer: A product demo, a how-it-works piece, a step-by-step, a before-and-after, an app or service shown in use. The audience is deciding whether it is for them.
'anime' (both) - Anime: The user wants a scene, a person, a product or a photo re-drawn as Japanese animation. The identity of a character or a product stays; the medium changes completely.
'illustration' (video) - Illustration: An explainer that should feel like a magazine illustration, a storybook moment, a comic panel that comes alive, a flat vector scene for a product story, a watercolour mood piece.
'toon3d' (both) - 3D toon: A character piece in the manner of an animated feature, a product turned into a designed CGI key visual, a mascot brought to life, an explainer with a friendly 3D cast.
'pixel' (both) - Pixel art: A retro game look for a product, a mascot as a sprite, a short scene that plays like a cutscene from an indie game, a pixel banner or key visual.
'3d' (3d: generate_3d only) - 3D model: A character, a prop, a product or a piece of environment that has to exist as geometry: to drop into Blender, Unity, Unreal or a browser game, to print, to show in AR, to animate as a rigged humanoid. Anything where the deliverable is a file with polygons, not a picture.
Leave EMPTY for a universal render. Unknown ids are ignored. list_skills returns the same list with the current snapshot; get_skill reads a playbook's interview and checks.

effectOptions.description: Options for the effect, JSON {"questionId":"optionId"} using the ids from list_effects, e.g. {"place":"pyramids"}. Omit to take the effect's defaults.

ratio.description: Aspect ratio, e.g. '9:16', '16:9', '1:1'. Leave empty for the default. Some models refuse some ratios - call list_models when unsure.

durationSeconds.description: Clip length in seconds. Allowed steps differ per model and are snapped UP to the next tier, which is what gets charged. Leave empty for the model's default.

resolution.description: Ignored: every model renders at its own fixed resolution. For a cheap 480p try use `draft`; for 1080p on 'seedance-2-5' pass quality='hd' or finalize a draft.

referenceImageUrls.description: Public HTTPS URLs of reference images. One image turns this into image-to-video. How many the model takes differs sharply - 'seedance-2-5' takes 30, most others 4 - so call list_models when it matters. They must be reachable from the internet.

startImageUrl.description: KEYFRAME ANCHORS. 'startImageUrl' is the literal first frame of the clip and 'endImageUrl' the frame it must land on - use them to chain shots so the seam is invisible. This is a SEPARATE mode at the provider, not two more references: with a pair attached you may NOT pass referenceImageUrls, referenceVideoUrls, referenceAudioUrls, imageRole, bloggerId, studioId or productId in the same call, and the request is refused before a single credit is spent. 'endImageUrl' only works on models that accept a target end frame - list_models flags them as supports_last_frame - and on most of them it needs 'startImageUrl' alongside it.

endImageUrl.description: Public HTTPS URL of the frame the clip must land on. Usually needs startImageUrl alongside it; 'minimax' also accepts it ALONE - the clip then starts wherever the model likes and simply has to land on this frame.

referenceVideoUrls.description: Public HTTPS URLs of reference VIDEO clips, at most 3 (mp4/mov, up to 200 MB each). The model follows their motion, camera and pacing - not their people or places. Only 'seedance-2-5', 'seedance', 'minimax', 'wan3', 'wan3-prime', 'wan' and 'omni' take them (15 s per clip; omni 3 s), and 'kling-motion' REQUIRES exactly one clip of a person performing the motion plus one reference image of the character - the output is as long as the clip. A clip from list_generations of this account is a valid URL. Bind clips in the prompt the way the model docs say (@Video1 / Video 1 / reference video 1).

referenceAudioUrls.description: Public HTTPS URLs of reference AUDIO tracks (mp3/wav). The model borrows their voice, timbre and rhythm. Only 'seedance-2-5' takes them today (up to 10), and the provider needs at least one photo or clip alongside the audio. Bind each in the prompt as @Audio1.

imageRole.description: What a SINGLE reference photo is for. 'reference' = it shows the hero, the place or the product and the model builds its own opening frame (Seedance, Veo, MiniMax, Wan, Omni, Kling 3.0); 'start_frame' = the photo is the literal first frame the clip grows out of (image-to-video); 'auto' (default) = reference on every model that has the mode (Seedance, Veo, MiniMax, Wan, Omni, Kling 3.0), start_frame elsewhere (Runway, HappyHorse, Grok) - so say 'start_frame' explicitly when the user wants THIS photo animated as the opening frame. Two or more photos are always references.

seed.description: Optional seed. Only one model in the lineup honours it; leave empty by default.

bloggerId.description: Id of the user's AI BLOGGER (list_brand_assets kind 'avatar', status 'ready') - their persistent brand character. Pass it whenever the clip or image should feature that character: the platform then injects the blogger's canonical reference photos and its appearance passport (CHARACTER LOCK) itself, so the face stays the same across every render. Describe the character in your prompt consistently with the passport. Identity never changes - face, hair, build, age, marks; only the render medium follows the requested style.

avatarId.description: Deprecated alias of bloggerId - the same AI Blogger id under its old name. Pass bloggerId instead.

studioId.description: Id of the user's LOCATION from list_brand_assets. Pass it to stage the scene in that exact place: the platform injects its canonical reference and scene passport (SCENE LOCK). Keep its signage, logos and lettering in frame.

productId.description: Id of the user's PRODUCT from list_brand_assets. Pass it whenever the product must appear: the platform injects its photos as references and merges its name and description into the prompt. Keep the product's shape, colours and labels accurate - it stays the hero of the shot.

draft.description: DRAFT mode, 'seedance-2-5' only: a cheap 480p take (about 18 credits per 5 s instead of 41) to test an idea before paying for the real render. Within 7 days finalize_draft re-renders the SAME take (same seed, prompt and references) in 1080p. A draft cannot be extended or upscaled and cannot use startImageUrl/endImageUrl. list_models flags models with supports_draft.

quality.description: 'hd' renders straight to 1080p on models that support it ('seedance-2-5', about 100 credits per 5 s instead of 41; list_models flags supports_hd). Leave empty for the standard tier. Models that already render 1080p (Kling, Veo, Wan) need nothing here.

guideId.description: Only when you repeat a recipe read with get_mira_guide: its guide_id. Pass it together with guideBlockId - this credits the guide's author and lets Mira treat the author's shared blockout playblast (ref_video_urls) as a blockout. Leave empty otherwise.

guideBlockId.description: Only with guideId: the block_id of the get_mira_guide block whose recipe you repeat.

direction.description: DIRECTION - the user's own camera, light and look picks, as JSON with bank keys (never write the keys into the prompt; the pipeline expands each into its description): camera_moves (up to 4, in order within the shot), camera_style, camera (body), lens, focal (14|24|35|50|85|135), aperture (f1_4|f2_8|f4|f11), lighting (a scheme) or lights [{color hex, brightness 0-100, softness 0-100, from top|front|left|right|back|bottom}], grade, stock, palette or colors [hex, dominant first], genre, era, tempo. The keys are listed in the mira-craft skill (camera.md, light.md, look.md, direction.md). Omit to let the pipeline decide.

filmProjectId.description: AI FILM STUDIO: filmProjectId from film_list_projects to render INTO that team project - the take lands in the project's bin for the whole team and is PAID FROM THE WORKSPACE OWNER'S BALANCE within the user's monthly limit, not from the user's own credits. Needs the editor role. Omit for a normal personal render.

elementIds.description: AI FILM STUDIO, with filmProjectId: elementIds of the project's cast from film_list_elements - up to 3 characters, 1 location and 1 prop per take. The platform injects each element's canonical references and passport, so the same character, place and prop stay identical across the team's takes. Describe them in the prompt consistently with their passports. Use these instead of bloggerId / studioId / productId there.

refAssetIds.description: AI FILM STUDIO, with filmProjectId: assetIds of finished takes from film_list_assets to use as reference images (the platform fetches them itself - do not pass their URLs as referenceImageUrls).

brandMode.description: AI MARKETING STUDIO campaigns only (with filmProjectId): off | accents (default) | lock (video: the grade follows the brand palette). The campaign's brand kit is applied by the server; never write the logo or hex codes into the prompt.

placementId.description: AI MARKETING STUDIO campaigns only: placementId from mkt_list_styles (reels, stories, ig_feed_portrait, ig_feed_square, youtube…) - sets the aspect ratio for that placement.

styleId.description: AI MARKETING STUDIO campaigns only: styleId from mkt_list_styles - brings the style's recipe, skill and defaults.

hookId.description: AI MARKETING STUDIO campaigns only, video: hookId from mkt_list_styles - the opening beat.

hookText.description: AI MARKETING STUDIO campaigns only, video: the opening beat in your words (max 300 chars).

settingId.description: AI MARKETING STUDIO campaigns only, video: settingId from mkt_list_styles - where it happens.

settingText.description: AI MARKETING STUDIO campaigns only, video: the place in your words (max 300 chars).

tools.name: direct_video
tools.title: Direct a video from a preset
tools.description:
Renders ONE finished clip (up to 30 s) from a DIRECT preset ('Direct Your Video'): the preset's director turns the user's answers, cast, photos and song into the film and writes the prompt itself - you write no prompt. SPENDS THE USER'S CREDITS: the preset's price for the chosen length.
Flow: call list_direct_presets first; ask the user that preset's questions conversationally (required ones must be answered, optional ones only if the user cares); quote the price for the length and get a yes; then call this.
Photos, the song and the ad clip must be the user's OWN files: URLs returned by upload_reference_image or create_upload, or of the user's own generations (list_generations). Any other link is refused before a single credit is spent. A saved AI Blogger goes into characters as bloggerId (list_brand_assets kind 'avatar'). Preset 'ad-remake' takes videoUrl, mode, language, note and keepAudio instead of answers.
Video takes several minutes: this returns a generation_id immediately; call wait_for_generation.

preset.description:
Id of the DIRECT preset - a ready-made director that turns the user's answers into ONE finished clip up to 30 s. The preset writes the prompt itself, so there is no prompt here: ask the user its questions and pass the answers. Fields marked * are required; choice fields take an option id; characters and images give min-max counts; every preset runs on its own model.
'short-film' Short Film - A whole story, start to finish, in one clip. 15|30 s (default 30), 16:9|9:16|1:1 (default 16:9). Fields: story* (text, up to 5000 chars); style (choice cinematic|experimental|monochrome|animated|artistic, default cinematic, or the user's own words); characters (characters 0-4); refs (images 0-4, reference).
'music-video' Music Video - Your song, cut to the beat. 15|30 s (default 15), 9:16|16:9|1:1 (default 9:16). Fields: type* (choice narrative|performance|visualizer, default narrative); song* (the user's song); characters (characters 0-1); direction (text, up to 500 chars).
'real-estate' Real Estate - Listing photos into a smooth property tour. 15|30 s (default 30), 16:9|9:16 (default 16:9). Fields: photos* (images 3-20, property); preferences (text, up to 500 chars).
'product-ads' Product Ads - Studio-quality ads made to stop the scroll. 10|15|30 s (default 15), 9:16|16:9|1:1 (default 9:16). Fields: product* (images 1-8, product); name* (text, up to 60 chars); why* (text, up to 300 chars).
'ad-remake' Ad Remake - Any ad, remade with your product. Kind remake: the user's existing ad clip is remade with their product - pass the ad clip, the product photos as images of field 'product' (up to 8) and at most one character; optional mode close|flex, language, note, keepAudio. Length follows the source ad, up to 30 s.
'social-content' Social Content - You on camera, your story, ready to post. 10|15|30 s (default 15), 9:16|1:1 (default 9:16). Fields: characters* (characters 1-1); topic* (text, up to 500 chars); vibe (choice casual|funny|inspiring|chill|luxury, default casual, or the user's own words).
'ugc-ads' UGC Ads - Real people, real moments, made to sell. 10|15|30 s (default 15), 9:16|1:1 (default 9:16). Fields: product (images 0-8, product); name* (text, up to 60 chars); selling_points* (text, up to 500 chars); characters (characters 0-1).
'micro-drama' Micro Drama - Short, addictive, made for vertical. 15|30 s (default 30), 9:16 (default 9:16). Fields: characters* (characters 1-4); plot* (text, up to 5000 chars); vibe (choice romance|thriller|comedy|horror, or the user's own words).
'brand-film' Brand Film - Say what your brand stands for. We bring it to life. 15|30 s (default 30), 16:9|9:16|1:1 (default 16:9). Fields: brand_name* (text, up to 60 chars); stands_for* (text, up to 500 chars); feeling (text, up to 100 chars); refs (images 0-4, reference).
'explainer' Explainer - Explainers that make things click. 15|30 s (default 30), 16:9|9:16|1:1 (default 16:9). Fields: topic* (text, up to 500 chars); audience (text, up to 100 chars); style (choice cinematic|whiteboard|minimal|illustrated, default minimal); refs (images 0-4, reference).
'film-trailer' Film Trailer - Every story begins with a feeling. 15|30 s (default 30), 16:9|9:16 (default 16:9). Fields: concept* (text, up to 500 chars); genre (choice comedy|thriller|action|sci-fi|romance|horror|drama|fantasy, or the user's own words); characters (characters 0-3); refs (images 0-4, reference).
Prices differ per preset and length - list_direct_presets returns them with the live catalog. An unknown id is refused before any credits are spent.

answers.description: Answers to the preset's text and choice questions as {"fieldId": "answer"}: text fields take the user's own words (their language is fine); choice fields take an option id from list_direct_presets, or the user's own words where the field is `custom`. An omitted choice takes its default.

characters.description: The cast, for presets with a characters field, in order of importance. Each is ONE of bloggerId (a ready AI Blogger from list_brand_assets), imageUrl (the user's own photo of the person) or description (who it is, in words), plus an optional role name.

bloggerId.description: Id of a ready AI BLOGGER (list_brand_assets kind 'avatar'). Use exactly one of bloggerId, imageUrl, description.

avatarId.description: Deprecated alias of bloggerId - the same AI Blogger id. Pass bloggerId instead.

imageUrl.description: URL of a photo of this person from create_upload / upload_reference_image / the user's own generations.

description.description: Who this is, in words (up to 500 characters), when there is no AI Blogger or photo.

name.description: Optional role name the story uses, up to 40 characters, e.g. 'Anna'.

images.description: Photos for the preset's images fields, each {field, url}, e.g. {"field":"product", "url":"..."}. Several photos of one field go as several entries, in the user's order (a property tour follows it). URLs must be the user's own uploads or generations.

field.description: Id of the preset's images field, e.g. 'product', 'photos', 'refs'.

url.description: URL from create_upload / upload_reference_image / the user's own generations.

songUrl.description: music-video: URL of the user's song (mp3/wav/m4a, up to 50 MB), uploaded with create_upload kind 'audio'. The clip is cut to it and the song is laid over the result.

songStart.description: music-video: where in the song the clip starts, in seconds. Default 0.

duration.description: Clip length in seconds - one of the preset's durations. Empty = the preset's default. Ignored by 'ad-remake', whose length follows the source ad.

ratio.description: Aspect ratio - one of the preset's ratios, e.g. '9:16'. Empty = the preset's default ('ad-remake': as the original).

projectId.description: Optional id of the user's project (folder) to file the result under. Leave empty otherwise.

videoUrl.description: ad-remake only: URL of the ad to remake (2-120 s; only its first 30 s are used) - create_upload kind 'video' or one of the user's own video generations.

mode.description: ad-remake only: 'flex' (default - keep the story, pace, look and hook, free framing) or 'close' (repeat the shots and timing almost frame by frame).

language.description: ad-remake only: ISO 639-1 language of the speech in the result, e.g. 'en'. Empty keeps the original language.

note.description: ad-remake only: the user's wish for the remake, up to 500 characters.

keepAudio.description: ad-remake only: lay the ORIGINAL soundtrack (music and voices) over the result. Cannot be combined with language.

tools.name: list_models
tools.title: List available generation models
tools.description: Lists the image, video and 3D models this account can use right now, plus the accepted aspect ratios, clip durations and resolutions, and for 3D models their inputs, formats, quality tiers and credit prices. Call it when you are unsure whether a model name is valid, or when the user asks what is available. Model names are validated server-side: an unknown name silently falls back to the registry default rather than failing, so checking here is how you avoid rendering with the wrong model. An empty model3d_models list means 3D generation is switched off on this deployment. `video_model_specs` carries what each video model actually accepts - how many reference photos, clips and audio tracks, whether it takes a target end frame, whether its clips can be extended and in which directions (extend_directions), whether it has a cheap 480p draft that finalize_draft turns into 1080p (supports_draft), whether it renders straight to 1080p with quality='hd' (supports_hd). `image_model_ratios` lists image models with their OWN ratio set (nano-banana-2.1 adds the panoramic 21:9, 4:1, 8:1, 1:4, 1:8); every other image model takes `aspect_ratios`. Those caps differ in multiples between models, so read them here rather than guessing.

tools.name: generate_image
tools.title: Generate an image
tools.description:
Renders an image from a text prompt, optionally guided by reference photos. SPENDS THE USER'S CREDITS: 3 per image, 1 on muse-image, 4 on seedream-5-pro or nano-banana-2.1, 6 on ideogram-4.5, 8 on the premium models (nano-banana-pro, gpt-image-2.5-sunburst). Say what it will cost before running a batch.
Write the prompt in ENGLISH and make it complete and vivid. Everything you state is kept word for word - the subject, the setting, the moment, any lettering - while a pipeline of specialists fills only the craft slots you left empty (lighting scheme and its source, lens and framing, grade and texture) before the image is rendered. So state what you care about and leave the rest. Compose for the requested aspect ratio.
Generation is asynchronous: this returns a generation_id immediately. Poll get_generation, or call wait_for_generation to block until the image is ready.

prompt.description: Final, detailed visual prompt in English. Your decisions are kept verbatim; unstated craft (light, optics, grade) is filled in before rendering.

model.description:
Model to render the image. CHOOSE ONE DELIBERATELY, BY WHAT THE IMAGE NEEDS.
SELECTION RULE - apply it every single call:
1. Name the ONE thing that decides this image: text in frame? an exact tall ratio? the same product or person across a series? print-grade detail? Take the model listed for it.
2. If none of them is true - an ordinary photoreal visual - the answer is 'gpt-image-2'.
3. Never repeat the same key call after call out of habit; re-read the brief each time.
Every model costs 3 credits per image EXCEPT 'muse-image' (1), 'seedream-5-pro' (4), 'nano-banana-2.1' (4), 'ideogram-4.5' (6) and the premium tier at 8 credits: 'nano-banana-pro' and 'gpt-image-2.5-sunburst' - pick the pricier ones only when their strengths below are actually needed:
'gpt-image-2' - the strongest at holding a detailed commercial brief with many requirements at once (exact copy + brand colours + camera angle + lighting + what must not change), at photorealistic products, materials and skin, and at preserving product geometry, packaging and logos. The right default for e-commerce packshots and structured ad layouts.
'gpt-image-2.5-flare' - the newest GPT image family at the fast 3-credit tier: the same brief-holding and product fidelity as gpt-image-2, plus legible in-image text in ANY script including Cyrillic, and it renders the EXACT requested ratio. Pick it for a text-bearing post, story or banner and for faithful multi-photo edits when the premium tier is not needed.
'gpt-image-2.5-sunburst' - premium (8 credits): the same family at its highest quality, sharper detail, richer light and the tightest control over edits - it changes only what you name and keeps the rest of the reference. Pick it for production-ready campaign creative, polished product imagery and edits of the user's own photo that must stay faithful.
'nano-banana-pro' - premium (8 credits): legible in-image text in any language including Cyrillic, one design that must exist in several languages, infographics and diagrams, and many reference photos blended while several people stay recognisable.
'nano-banana-2.1' - 4 credits: Google's newer, faster Nano Banana at half the premium price - sharp legible in-image text in any language including Cyrillic, infographics, diagrams and multi-block layouts, on the EXACT requested ratio. It is the ONLY model that also takes the panoramic ratios 21:9, 4:1, 8:1 (wide banners, headers, strips) and 1:4, 1:8 (tall scrolls, skyscraper banners) - pick it whenever the user wants one of those shapes. Describe a panorama along its long side (what sits left, centre, right). Prefer 'nano-banana-pro' only for the hardest multi-person blends and maximum polish.
'seedream-4' - keeps one product or character consistent across several reference photos. Pick it when the same SKU or person must appear in multiple scenes and stay identical.
'seedream-4k' - same model at 4K (up to 4096px). Pick it only when the output is a print, a large-format or hero visual where fine detail is inspected; for a social post it is waste.
'seedream-5-pro' - 4 credits: ByteDance's flagship at true 2K on the EXACT requested ratio - the most photographic skin, fabric, glass and metal in the lineup, and one product or person kept identical across several references. Pick it for premium product and lifestyle stills and close-ups where texture is inspected; keep on-image text short.
'muse-image' - 1 credit, the cheapest: Meta's model that grounds itself in live web and image search, so real places, landmarks, products and current designs come out recognisable when you name them. Pick it for a scene that must show something real and specific, and for cheap drafts and variations.
'ideogram-4.5' - 6 credits: the typography and graphic-design specialist - posters, covers, packaging, signage, logos and editorial layouts where the lettering IS the design: exact words in quotes land where you place them, in the weight and type style you name, on the EXACT requested ratio. Pick it when the type and the layout are the point; short Cyrillic lines render cleanly too, but for long Cyrillic copy prefer 'gpt-image-2.5-flare'. With a photo attached it edits that photo (the first one) - add a headline, swap a label, restyle the background.
'flux' - the fastest. Pick it for quick drafts, mood exploration and variations. Its in-image text is the weakest of the lineup - never pick it for copy.
ASPECT RATIO OVERRIDES ALL OF THE ABOVE: 'gpt-image-2' and 'flux' return 2:3 for EVERY tall ratio, so a 9:16 story or a 4:5 feed post comes back the wrong shape. When the ratio must be exact, pick 'gpt-image-2.5-flare', 'gpt-image-2.5-sunburst', 'nano-banana-pro', 'nano-banana-2.1', 'seedream-5-pro', 'muse-image', 'ideogram-4.5' or 'seedream-4'/'seedream-4k'. Panoramic 21:9, 4:1, 8:1, 1:4 and 1:8 exist ONLY on 'nano-banana-2.1' - any other model renders them 1:1. Leave empty to fall back to 'gpt-image-2'. Call list_models to see what this account has.

skill.description:
Optional SKILL - a playbook for the genre and structure of the piece (not its medium; medium is `style`). The platform injects the playbook's doctrine into its prompt pipeline itself, so never restate or paraphrase it: pass the id and write the piece as the user described it. Pick by what the piece is FOR:
'ugc' (both) - UGC: A real person shows or talks about a product the way a customer would: a review, an unboxing, a short how-to, a testimonial, a "day with it" clip. Vertical, social, meant to sit between other people's phone videos and not stand out as paid.
'product' (both) - Product: A packshot, a product video, a marketplace card, a lifestyle scene where the product is in use but still the hero. Anything where a buyer needs to see exactly what they get.
'ads' (both) - Ads: Paid social creative, a launch teaser, a sale announcement, a static banner with a headline. The piece exists to make someone act, not to be admired.
'cinematic' (both) - Cinematic: A brand film, a teaser, a hero shot, a key visual, an atmospheric moment with a person, a place or a product. The piece is meant to be felt before it is understood.
'explainer' (video) - Explainer: A product demo, a how-it-works piece, a step-by-step, a before-and-after, an app or service shown in use. The audience is deciding whether it is for them.
'anime' (both) - Anime: The user wants a scene, a person, a product or a photo re-drawn as Japanese animation. The identity of a character or a product stays; the medium changes completely.
'illustration' (video) - Illustration: An explainer that should feel like a magazine illustration, a storybook moment, a comic panel that comes alive, a flat vector scene for a product story, a watercolour mood piece.
'toon3d' (both) - 3D toon: A character piece in the manner of an animated feature, a product turned into a designed CGI key visual, a mascot brought to life, an explainer with a friendly 3D cast.
'pixel' (both) - Pixel art: A retro game look for a product, a mascot as a sprite, a short scene that plays like a cutscene from an indie game, a pixel banner or key visual.
'3d' (3d: generate_3d only) - 3D model: A character, a prop, a product or a piece of environment that has to exist as geometry: to drop into Blender, Unity, Unreal or a browser game, to print, to show in AR, to animate as a rigged humanoid. Anything where the deliverable is a file with polygons, not a picture.

tools.name: adobe_command
tools.title: Run a named panel command
tools.description: Runs one of the panel's typed commands with a JSON input instead of raw ExtendScript. AFTER EFFECTS: list_compositions {}, get_composition_info {comp|name}, list_layers {comp} (index, type, in/out, 3D, parent, blend, track matte, effects, markers), create_composition {name,width,height,fps,duration}, add_text_layer {comp,text,name}, add_solid_layer {comp,color,name}, set_keyframe {comp,layer,property,time,value}, apply_effect {comp,layer,effect}, set_track_matte {comp,layer,matteLayer,mode: luma|luma_inverted|alpha|alpha_inverted}, set_keyframes {comp,layer,property (name, match name or Transform/Position), keys:[{time,value,ease}], ease} where ease is linear | hold | ease | in (arrive slowly at this key, like CSS ease-out on the move before it) | out (leave this key slowly) | {in,out} influence 0-100, add_marker {comp,time,comment,duration,layer?}, read_markers {comp,layer?}, precompose {comp,layers,name}, set_parent {comp,layer,parent}, set_time {comp,time}, set_work_area {comp,start,duration}, open_comp {comp}, save_project {}. `comp` defaults to the active composition; `layer` is a name or a 1-based index. Each mutating command is one undo step. PREMIERE PRO commands (seconds are sequence time unless said otherwise; the active sequence is the target): get_timeline {} (tracks with every clip: start/end, name, mediaPath, enabled, selected; fps, size, in/out, playhead), open_sequence {name}, set_playhead {seconds}, assemble_edit {name?, clips:[{source|url, in?, out?, track?, punch?, marker?}], width?, height?, fit?} - ONE call builds a NEW sequence matched to the first clip's footage, optionally reframed (1080x1920 for 9:16), with the whole ordered cut plan placed gaplessly (each clip starts at the real end of the previous one on its track; in/out are SOURCE seconds; `source` is a mediaPath from get_timeline, a project item name or a local file; `url` is downloaded first; linked audio follows; clips are fitted to the frame, punch 1.15-1.25 adds a light push-in), apply_cut_plan {clips:[...same], at?} - the same onto the ACTIVE sequence from `at` (default its end), apply_cuts {cuts:[{s,e}], mode: ripple|lift} - remove sequence ranges on all unlocked tracks (ripple closes the gaps), add_markers {markers:[{s, e?, name, comment?}]}, switch_multicam {segments:[{s,e,track}]} - inside each range only video track `track` (0-based) stays enabled, create_subclips {clips:[{s,e,name}]} - one named sequence per range, import_captions {path|url} - an .srt as a caption track, set_sequence_format {width,height,fit?,punch?}, fit_all_video {punch?}, save_project {}. Premiere SOUND and DELIVERY (panel 0.9.5+; audio tracks are 0-based: 0 = A1 speech, 1 = A2 music by default; `clip` is a 0-based index or a name): audio_gaps {track, max_pause (0.4)} - dead air between clips and the leading silence; recompact_audio {track, min_pause (0.25), max_pause (1.0), start?} - pauses clamped into the range, the speaker's rhythm kept, linked picture moved along; set_audio_level {track, clip, db}; audio_fade {track, clip, keys:[{t (s from the clip start), db}]}; duck_music {music_track (1), speech_track (0), duck_db (-15), ramp (0.3)} - level keys on the music under every speech clip; music_bed {path|url (e.g. an add_soundtrack / generate_audio result), track (1), start, fade_in (0.5), fade_out (2), overlap (1.5), duck (true), duck_db (-15), speech_track (0), level_db} - one call: trimmed to the content end, tiled with crossfades on track and track+1 when short, faded and ducked; refuses a bed track that already holds clips; import_mogrt {path|url, track (1), start} - returns its text_fields; set_mogrt_text {track, clip, text, param?}; export_sequence {output_path?, preset_path?} - the active sequence (in -> out when set) to an H.264 mp4 with the stock Match Source preset (a 9:16 sequence exports vertical), saved to ~/Movies/Mira by default; Premiere is busy until it is written. tools.name: draw_edit_video

tools.description: Draw to Edit: changes ONE marked area of a clip and keeps everything else - people, motion, camera, timing and sound (Seedance 2.5 edit, one pass, the result has the clip's length). The user marks WHERE on one frame of the clip (brush strokes, arrows, outlines, notes) and says WHAT to change in prompt (start with a verb: replace, remove, add, change). Pass the marked frame as frameImageUrl (a JPEG/PNG of that frame with the marks drawn on it), or the drawing alone as overlayImageUrl (a transparent PNG the size of the frame) - Mira then lays it over the frame at frameSeconds. Both must be uploaded to Mira first (upload_reference_image or create_upload). You cannot draw yourself: ask the user for the marked frame, or describe the area in words in prompt and use the clean frame. referenceImageUrl optionally shows how the new element must look. The clip is a Mira clip (sourceGenerationId) or an upload (libraryItemId) - pass exactly one - 4 to 30 s. Uploaded clips with real people may be refused by the model (moderation_blocked, refunded). SPENDS CREDITS per second of the clip by resolution: 480p 5, 720p (default) 10, 1080p 23 - see estimate_cost kind 'draw_edit' with model = resolution. Returns a new generation_id; call wait_for_generation.
